claim: Oslo Pass 2026 adult prices are 580 NOK (24h), 845 NOK (48h), 995 NOK (72h); child (6-17) 290/420/495 NOK; senior (67+) 465/675/795 NOK.

Oslo Pass covers 30+ museums (Munch, Folkemuseum, Kon-Tiki, Holmenkollen), unlimited Ruter transit (bus/tram/metro/local trains), the Bygdøy boat and ferries to inner Oslofjord islands (Hovedøya, Lindøya, Nakholmen, Bleikøya, Gressholmen, Langøyene).
quote: Boats out to Bygdøy and ferries to inner Oslofjord islands (Hovedøya, Lindøya, Nakholmen, Bleikøya, Gressholmen, Langøyene)

claim: Oslo Pass breaks even quickly for multi-museum visitors: 7 attractions plus transit cost 2,045 NOK pay-as-you-go vs 995 NOK with the 72-hour pass, but a standalone 24h Ruter zone 1 ticket is just 137 NOK for light sightseers.
quote: A sample itinerary visiting 7 major attractions plus transit cost 2,045 NOK without the pass versus 995 NOK with the 72-hour pass—saving over 1,000 NOK ... a standalone 24-hour transit pass costs just 137 NOK

claim: Flytoget Airport Express one-way adult fare from Oslo Airport Gardermoen to Oslo S is 268 NOK in 2026 (134 NOK reduced).
quote: The fare from Oslo Airport (Oslo S station) to Oslo Central Station is 268 NOK for adults and 134 NOK for discounted categories.

claim: The Vy regional train Gardermoen–Oslo S costs around 129 NOK and takes about 23 minutes, versus Flytoget at ~258 NOK in 19 minutes — Vy is roughly half the price for only 4 extra minutes, and the Vy ticket includes 2.5h of onward Oslo bus/tram/metro transfers.
quote: The Vy train from the airport costs 129 NOK ... and takes 23 minutes ... Your regional train ticket includes transfers to Oslo's buses, trams, and metro for 2.5 hours after purchase

claim: Torp Sandefjord (TRF) is connected to Oslo by Vy regional R11 trains roughly every hour plus a synchronised yellow shuttle bus to Torp station; total journey to central Oslo is about 1h45.
quote: more than 20 departures a day are available from Oslo to Torp Airport by train (R11) and shuttle bus in 1 hour and 45 minutes ... The shuttlebus awaits at Torp Station on most arrivals

claim: Torp-Ekspressen runs a coach service between Torp airport and Oslo central bus terminal in about 1h35, timed to flights as a direct alternative to the train+shuttle combo.
quote: Travel time from Torp to central Oslo is 1 hour 35 minutes

claim: Late-May Oslo is mild spring weather: daily highs around 15-16°C, lows 6-7°C, with ~50-80 mm rain spread across roughly 5 wet days in the month.
quote: In May, Oslo witnesses the full bloom of spring, with warmer temperatures ranging from a low of 6.5°C (43.7°F) to a high of 15.8°C (60.4°F)

claim: Oslo daylight in May lengthens from ~16h to ~18h20m by month's end; average May day is 17.1 hours with sunrise ~04:41 and sunset ~21:46, producing prolonged twilight 'white night' conditions by late May.
quote: day length increases by 2 hours, 15 minutes over the month - from 16 hours, 3 minutes on the first day to 18 hours, 19 minutes on the last day. The average day in Oslo during May has 17.1 hours of daylight, with sunrise at 4:41 AM and sunset at 9:46 PM

claim: Oslo sunsets near the summer solstice last about 75 minutes of bright twilight because of the city's high latitude, so 'darkness' in late May/early June is really an extended blue-hour rather than true night.
quote: In June, the sunset lasts about 75 minutes in Oslo

claim: Piknik i Parken (PiP) runs 11-13 June 2026 in Sofienbergparken, Grünerløkka, with David Byrne, TLC, Kings of Convenience, Caribou and De La Soul headlining.
quote: The event will be held from June 11-13, 2026 ... at Sofienbergparken in Oslo ... David Byrne, TLC, Kings of Convenience, Caribou, and De La Soul among the festival's headliners

claim: Oslo Pride 2026 runs 17-27 June, with Pride Park at Kontraskjæret opening 24 June and the main parade Saturday 27 June from Grønland.
quote: Oslo Pride 2026 runs from June 17-27 ... Pride Park opens from June 24 at Kontraskjæret with live music, food vendors, beer tents and a market ... The Pride Parade takes place on June 27, 2026

claim: Norwegian Wood is not on the 2026 calendar — the festival's last edition was 2017 and the organising company went bankrupt that year; revival attempts have failed.
quote: 2017 was the final year Norwegian Wood took place. The responsible company behind the festival declared bankruptcy in autumn of that year, and later attempts to revive it has proven unsuccessful.

claim: Færderseilasen, the world's largest overnight sailing race with ~600 boats, starts from Oslo on the second weekend of June — 12-13 June 2026 — making the harbour and Oslofjord visibly busy that weekend.
quote: Færderseilasen, also called Færder'n, is a regatta that is held on the second weekend in June by the Royal Norwegian Yacht Club

claim: Oslo Jazz Festival 2026 is 9-15 August — outside a late-May/early-June weekend window, so it is not a factor for this trip.
quote: Oslo Jazz Festival 2026 will run from 9–15 August 2026

claim: Fram Museum on Bygdøy is open daily year-round with extended summer hours 09:30-18:00 from 1 May to 30 September, so the Bygdøy museum cluster is in full summer mode by late May.
quote: October 1 – April 30: 10am – 5pm; May 1 – September 30: 9:30am – 6pm

claim: Norsk Folkemuseum's summer season runs 1 May - 30 September with live programming — costumed hosts, folk music and dance, farm animals — meaning a late-May visit gets the full open-air experience.
quote: the summer period (1 May – 30 September) featuring lively activities, music and dance, farm animals, and hosts in traditional costumes

claim: The seasonal passenger ferry to Bygdøy from Rådhusbrygge runs mid-March to mid-October; bus 30 from central Oslo is the year-round alternative, with an extra summer ferry from Aker Brygge.
quote: The ferry to Bygdøy runs from 15 March – 13 October. Bus 30 runs year round, plus a seasonal ferry from Aker Brygge in summer.

claim: Sentrum (around Karl Johans gate and Oslo S) is the most convenient base for first-time short trips — central to museums, transit and shopping, though noisier and pricier with less neighbourhood character.
quote: Sentrum is home to top Oslo attractions like Karl Johans gate ... It's a good place to stay if you're short on time and want to be within walking distance of museums, restaurants, shopping, and public transport. However, it can be noisy

claim: Aker Brygge/Tjuvholmen is Oslo's upscale waterfront base — walkable to the National Museum and Astrup Fearnley, internationally polished, and the most natural fit for a Michelin-anchored stay, though noticeably more expensive.
quote: Aker Brygge and Tjuvholmen are among Oslo's most posh and expensive areas ... lively, social and highly walkable, with easy access to the National Museum, Astrup Fearnley Museum and the harbourfront

claim: Bjørvika/Sørenga is Oslo's newest waterfront district around the Opera House, MUNCH and the Barcode towers, walkable and water-fronted but more dense, architectural and modern than the old town.
quote: Bjørvika is easy walkable, and you're never far from the water ... area around the Opera House, MUNCH Museum, Barcode district and Sørenga waterfront

claim: Grünerløkka is the hipster/creative base — independent cafés, vintage shops, street art and the Akerselva river walk — more local and alternative but further from the central Michelin-cluster restaurants.
quote: Grünerløkka has a distinctly hipster-oriented atmosphere ... known for independent cafés, vintage shops, bars, record stores, street art and a more alternative feel than western Oslo

claim: Syttende mai (17 May) brings ~100,000 people into central Oslo for the children's parade from Akershus Fortress to Rådhusplassen with full traffic closures, but it is finished well before a late-May weekend — by 28-31 May the city is back to normal operations.
quote: Some 100,000 people, many dressed up in national costumes, travel to the city centre to participate in the main festivities ... The children's parade starts at 10:00 from the main gate of Akershus Fortress, and ends at Rådhusplassen around 13:30
